anchors.a3: exists-but-citation-wrong: The paper is real, but the venue/year are wrong. Correct citation: G. Hinton, D. Sager, M. Upton, D. Boggs, D. Carmean, A. Kyker, P. Roussel, 'The Microarchitecture of the Pentium 4 Processor,' Intel Technology Journal, vol. 5, no. 1 (Q1 2001), pp. 5-25. No IEEE Micro vol. 21 (2007) version exists as far as I know.

sources.title: The Pentium Chronicles: The People, Passion, and Politics Behind Intel's Landmark Chips
sources.venue_or_publication: Wiley-Interscience / IEEE Press (book), Robert P. Colwell
sources.what_it_covers: First-person history of the Pentium and Pentium Pro (P5/P6) projects: schedule slips, first-silicon bugs, debug and recovery, and organizational failure modes.
sources.why_relevant: Canonical chip-project war-story book; complements the owned architecture papers with the failure-and-recovery human side of closure and bring-up.
sources.verification_hint: search: "The Pentium Chronicles" Colwell Wiley IEEE

sources.title: Closing the Gap: ASIC Design in the Silicon Sandbox
sources.what_it_covers: Practitioner's end-to-end ASIC physical design closure at 90-65nm: floorplanning, congestion, timing closure, CTS, power grid/IR drop, and signoff, with anecdotal failure modes and fixes.
sources.why_relevant: Directly on-topic for the registry: an ASIC design-closure book written by a working IC designer rather than an academic.
sources.verification_hint: search: "Closing the Gap: ASIC Design in the Silicon Sandbox" Mack McGraw-Hill

sources.title: Methodology for post-silicon verification of the Itanium 2 processor
sources.venue_or_publication: D. Josephson and B. Poorman, DesignCon 2003 (also cited to the 1st Silicon Debug Workshop, 2004; exact venue uncertain)
sources.what_it_covers: Real post-silicon fault isolation on Itanium 2: debug methodology and first-hand anecdotes of first-silicon failures, how they were isolated, and fixed.
sources.why_relevant: Rare named public source of genuine silicon bring-up war stories from a flagship microprocessor program.

sources.title: IBM POWER7 multicore server processor
sources.venue_or_publication: B. Sinharoy et al., IBM Journal of Research and Development, vol. 55, no. 3, 2011
sources.what_it_covers: Implementation of IBM's 45nm SOI eight-core server chip: clocking/PLL scheme, power management, and large-chip physical integration constraints.
sources.why_relevant: Successor-generation companion to the owned POWER4 papers; documents the next round of real large-chip implementation and closure constraints at IBM.
sources.verification_hint: search: Sinharoy POWER7 IBM Journal of Research and Development vol 55 no 3 2011
